title: One second before four hours
hook: Would a round-number finish change the pace you choose?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Recognize bunching just below a round-number target in a finish-time distribution.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Recognize bunching just below a round-number target in a finish-time distribution.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy finish histogram has 12 and 28 runners in the two bins before a target, and 10 and 10 after. How many finish before it? Toy inputs A=[12, 28, 10, 10]; B=[15, 15, 15, 15].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[40, 20, 18], [30, 30, 0]]. Labels: Before, After, Edge gap.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The same four bins can show a sharp target-edge difference or a smooth distribution. Bunching describes the shape; it does not by itself identify why individual runners changed pace.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Before−2=15, Before−1=15, After+1=15, After+2=15. What is Before? Answer: 30.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Before−2=15, Before−1=15, After+1=15, After+2=15. What is Before?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 30. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Marathon finishing times bunch just under round numbers like 4:00, which act as reference points (Allen, Dechow, Pope & Wu, 2017).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Recognize bunching just below a round-number target in a finish-time distribution.
